description: A long line containing 'and' that is one errand and must not split.
content: Pick up the replacement hydraulic filter and gasket kit for the tractor at the dealer on Route 40 before they close
notes: The counterweight to segmentation-compound-line. 'Filter and gasket kit' is one purchase at one place in one trip; splitting it produces two errands the user must reconcile by hand. A rule that splits on 'and' passes fixture 19 and fails this one; a rule that never splits passes this and fails 19. The pair is the actual test, and neither is meaningful alone. Long enough to be a plausible wrapped line, which is the shape a naive line-based segmenter handles correctly and a naive conjunction-based one does not.
